editorial_note: The text remarks that 'probably the Seals of Earls should be made of Iron, and those of Presidents in mixture either of Copper and Silver, or of Silver and Mercury; as otherwise the Metal of one Planet, Mars, is excluded from the List.' This is an editorial conjecture in the source, not a settled correspondence.

binding_times_by_rank.times: From 9 till 12 o'clock at Noon, and from 3 till Sunset
From 3 in the afternoon till 9 at Night, and from 9 at Night till Sunrise
From Sunrise till Noonday in Clear Weather
From Dawning of Day till Sunrise, or from 4 o'clock till Sunset
Any time, excepting Twilight at Night, unless the King whom they are under be Invocated
Any hour of the Day, so it be in Woods, or in any other places whither men resort not, or where no noise is

moon_observations: The text says the best days are when the Moon is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, or 14 days old, 'as Solomon saith', and no other days be profitable.
source: De Laurence 1916, 'Observations' (p. 34 of PDF) and classified list footnote (p. 35 of PDF)
